1000114.etyen: From French accent (“accent, manner or tone of speech”), from Middle French accent, from Old French acent, from Latin accentus (“accent, tone, accentuation”), past participle of accinō (“sing to, sing along”), from both ad- (“to”), from ad (“to, towards”), from Proto-Italic *ad (“toward, to, on, up to, for”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd (“to, at”) + and from canō (“to sing, recite, play”), from Proto-Italic *kanō (“to sing”), from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂n- (“to sing”).

en.g: Serbia and Montenegro; a former country on the Balkan Peninsula, in southeastern Europe, with Belgrade as its capital
x: Serbia og Montenegro ble oppløst i 2006.
Serbia and Montenegro was dissolved in 2006.
Serbia og Montenegro var i perioden 1992–2006 en forbundsrepublikk i Sørøst-Europa, på Balkanhalvøya.
Serbia and Montenegro was a federal republic in Southeastern Europe, on the Balkan Peninsula, from 1992 to 2006.

1000626.etyen:
From Serbia (“Serbia”) + og (“and”) + Montenegro (“Montenegro”), translating the native official name Serbo-Croatian Srbija i Crna Gora (“Serbia and Montenegro”). The state adopted the name in 2003, replacing Forbundsrepublikken Jugoslavia (“the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia”).
Parallel formations include Norwegian Nynorsk Serbia og Montenegro, Danish Serbien og Montenegro, Swedish Serbien och Montenegro, German Serbien und Montenegro, Dutch Servië en Montenegro and English Serbia and Montenegro.

1004210.etyen: abderitt + -isk, first part from German Abderit (“Abderite”), from Latin Abderita, Abderites, from Ancient Greek Ἀβδηρίτης (Abdērítēs), from Ἄβδηρα (Ábdēra, “Abdera”), from a Phoenician word + -ῑ́της (-ī́tēs, “demonymic suffix”), a back-formation of πολῑ́της (polī́tēs), from both πόλις (pólis, “city, community”), from Proto-Hellenic *ptólis (“city”), from Proto-Indo-European *tpólHis, from *tpelH- (“fortification, city”) + and from -της (-tēs, forms demonyms), from Proto-Hellenic *-tās, probably from Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂ and *-tós (forms verbal adjectives). Last part from Old Norse -iskr

en.g: a male given name from Old Norse, equivalent to English Torgeir

1004722.etyen:
An alternative spelling of Torgeir, with silent h. Ultimately from Old Norse Þórgeirr, from Þórr (“Thor”) + geirr (“spear”), literally “Thor's spear”.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Thorgeir, Faroese Torgeir, Icelandic Þorgeir, Swedish Torgeir and Danish Torgeir (“male given name”).

1004978.etyen: dato (“date”) + veksel (“bill of exchange”), literally “date bill of exchange”. dato (“date”) is ultimately from Latin datō, the ablative singular of datum (“date; given thing”), a nominalization of datus (“given”), the perfect passive participle of dō (“to give”), from Proto-Italic *didō (“to give”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃- (“to give”). veksel (“bill of exchange”) is borrowed from German Wechsel (“change, exchange; bill of exchange”), from Middle High German wëhsel, from Old High German wehsal, from Proto-Germanic *wihslaz (“change, exchange”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Eu
